source_findings.claim: compute_request_digest is NOT injective; the canonical request digest can collide
source_findings.status: ESTABLISHED by construction, independently reproduced read-only

evidence.formula: telegram_store.ml:131-133 renders read_set as "read:" ^ key ^ ":" ^ version ^ ":" ^ sha ^ "\n" with NO escaping of ':' or '\n'
evidence.enabling_condition: telegram_store.ml:692 key_valid k = String.length k > 0 && String.length k <= max_key_bytes — LENGTH ONLY, no charset constraint
evidence.collision: ONE entry {key="a:0:\nread:b", version=0, sha=""} renders byte-identically to TWO entries {key="a",0,""} and {key="b",0,""}
evidence.independent_reproduction: both renderings hashed to 14a020d5d7bbdcabe75241097d0aaca229d4244577f700dd27db226f2324f29a; cmp byte-identical
evidence.operator_supplied_full_preimage_hash: 77fea106a7708ba141329912afdfa2267b63d46aaed9e38a4c4dfa1c4ad179c6 — NOT re-derived here because the exact op string was not stated; the collision does not depend on it

source_findings.consequence: The digest is used as the idempotency/replay key (receipts.request_digest). A non-injective digest means two semantically different requests can be accepted as replays of one another, or a replay check can wrongly match. This is an integrity defect, not a formatting nit.
source_findings.scope_limit: Formulation collision only. No DB write and no native apply was executed by this review.
source_findings.required_correction: Make the canonical form injective: length-prefix every variable-length field (e.g. decimal-length ':' bytes), or restrict key to a charset excluding ':' and '\n' AND prove the restriction in a law. Prefer length-prefixing — a charset restriction is a second invariant that can drift from the formula. Add a regression law asserting the operator's exact collision pair hashes differently.

source_findings.evidence: telegram_store.ml:425 initialize_new executes a multi-statement DDL via exec_sql then FIVE separate insert_meta calls (schema, bot_id, generation, reserved_rows, reserved_receipts) with no BEGIN;/COMMIT;. The file's first BEGIN; is at line 499 and belongs to read_keys (line 483).
source_findings.consequence: A failure or crash between the DDL and the last insert_meta leaves a database with all tables and triggers present but incomplete meta — a half-initialized store that later code may read as structurally valid.
source_findings.required_correction: Wrap schema + all metadata seeding in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT with ROLLBACK on any error, matching the discipline already used by read_keys/apply at lines 499/583/640. Add a negative law: induced failure after DDL must leave NO usable store.
